## The test

What you built, on what, for how long. Numbers — services, requests per minute, rows, routes.
This paragraph is what separates a review from a rewritten pricing page, so be specific.

## Where Tool A pulled ahead

Two or three concrete wins with evidence. A benchmark number, a line count, a time-to-ship
figure. Say what caused the difference, not just that it exists.

## Where Tool B is genuinely better

Same treatment, honestly. A review where one side has no advantages is a review nobody believes.

## Cost

Real numbers at a stated scale. State the team size and the usage assumptions, because the answer
inverts at different sizes and the reader needs to map it onto themselves.

## How to choose

Two or three paragraphs, each starting with the situation rather than the tool: "Pick Tool A if…".
End with the honest hybrid or third option if one exists — there usually is one.
